purpose: The bench servos are the printed leg's IDs 1 (knee), 2 (worm) and 3 (belt/hip), not IDs 10-12. The bus scan in the robot-link firmware found them. This load puts the leg's own commissioning profile behind the ESP32 host pins.
motor_supply_off_reported_by_operator: Operator: 'supply off, p4 unplugged' just before the load. The P4's USB port was absent.
fpga_image: Tang repo bridge-calibration recipe (RELEASE_TX=1, SAFETY_ENABLE=1, SAFETY_FIRST_ID=1, SAFETY_COUNT=3, CALIBRATION=1, SAFETY_FEEDBACK_TIMEOUT=20000000 (400 ms), SAFETY_COMMAND_TIMEOUT=30000000 (600 ms)) with the host UART on G7 (host_rx) and G8 (host_tx). Supervisor profile 8, the same as the leg's deployment-v8 image ae912f43; only the host pins differ.
constraints_diff_from_tang_bridge_safety: Only host_rx B3 -> G7 and host_tx C3 -> G8

rtl_sources.repo: ~/projects/sipeed-tang-primer-25k at 3733582 with uncommitted changes. All five sources predate the v8 image (2026-09-22 21:20), so the RTL is the same as v8.

timing: nextpnr: PASS at 50 MHz (worst reported 70.80 MHz)

tests_before_load.tang: make sim-calibration: PASS (SYNC length predicates; multi-axis calibration arming; continuous encoder; servo modes; calibration profile: outward-only window, PWM cap, ID isolation, command gating, watchdog, S2, temperature; reply survives inter-byte pause)
tests_before_load.tang: make sim-safety: PASS (21 safety cases; UART safety; released TX during reply)
tests_before_load.robot-link cosim: Not applicable: the robot-link engine does not send travel windows, so this profile refuses to arm it. Motion goes through the Rust calibration panel over the TCP tunnel.

programming: SRAM only; openFPGALoader -b tangprimer25k, DONE (22:59:49Z to 22:59:52Z)
readback: Supervisor status over Wi-Fi through the P4's TCP tunnel, 2026-10-08 19:17 local: [8, 1, 9, 254, 0, 0, 0, 0, 60, 90, 126, 208, 7]. That is profile 8, latched with reason 9 (the usual load-time latch), nothing armed or fresh, and limits 60 C, 9.0-12.6 V, current 2000, matching the leg's deployment-v8 readback and the Rust calibration panel's profile check.

host.firmware: firmware/robot-link/esp32/build/robot_link.bin: first ID 1, mask 0x7, 2 s status log, bus scan, station mode on the home network, esp_hosted pinned ^2.12.12 (resolved to 2.12.13); page STOP is written straight to the FPGA while the tunnel or bus scan owns the UART

leg_before_load: Read through the previous image (reads are allowed to any ID), 2026-10-08 18:5x local: ID 1 11.1 V pos 2822 35 C; ID 2 11.1 V pos 1347 34 C; ID 3 11.1 V pos 2291 34 C. No motion commanded.
note: SRAM image: a dock power cycle reverts to its flash image. Reload with a new receipt, supply off, P4 unplugged.
tunnel_latency: 200 FPGA status round trips over Wi-Fi and the tunnel: 0 lost; median 7.7 ms, p90 12.9 ms, p99 22.6 ms, max 26.6 ms. A 90 s ping: 90/90, median 4 ms, max 35 ms. With esp_hosted 3.0.9 on the host, the station data path stalled within a minute.
stop_while_tunnel_held: 2026-10-08 19:20 local: with the tunnel held, POST /api/stop on the P4 produced two FPGA STOP replies on the tunnel: [8, 1, 10, 254], latched, host stop. The third copy was ignored while the bridge was busy.
